articles.title: ‘Sentimental Value’ Star Anders Danielsen Lie and Anne Marie Ottersen Inducted Into the Haugesund Walk of Fame: ‘It Feels Full Circle’
articles.summary: Norwegian actors Anders Danielsen Lie and Anne Marie Ottersen were inducted into the Haugesund Walk of Fame.. The unveiling taking place during the first weekend of this year’s Norwegian Intl.
body: “I think I dreamed of becoming a great actor when I was a young adult, but I abandoned that dream when I started med school. It was Joachim Trier’s first film that restarted my career,” he said.
“I think there are several ‘before’ and ‘after’ moments in my career, with the first being ‘Reprise’. If it weren’t for that film, I would never have worked as an actor.”

While “Oslo, August 31st” was probably “the biggest turning point” in his career, smash hits “The Worst Person in the World” and “Sentimental Value” – also directed by Trier – introduced him to an even bigger audience.

“It’s always hard to say exactly why a film is loved by the audience, but they both tell stories that are relatable to many people. They are very entertaining films, but they also have an almost therapeutic quality to them,” he noted, adding: “I’m a bit surprised I have an international career, because I’ve always been ambivalent about acting – but hopefully that adds an extra layer of complexity to my work!”

articles.title: Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Triumphs Again in Fourth Weekend With $39 Million, ‘Insidious 6’ Launches to $25 Million
articles.summary: Long may Peter Parker reign! Sony’s Marvel adventure “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” continues to dominate at the box office, collecting $39 million in its fourth weekend of release. Despite a smattering of newcomers, Spidey remained at No.
body: With no sign of slowing down, the newest “Spider-Man” is primed to eventually overtake “The Force Awakens” as the biggest movie ever at the domestic box office — and could even be the first to clear $1 billion in North America. Meanwhile, “Brand New Day” is the third-highest grossing movie in history in terms of worldwide grosses, behind just 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.9 billion) and “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.7 billion) and ahead of 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion).

“The Odyssey” landed at No. 3 with a remarkable $19.5 million in its sixth frame, a decline of just 17% from the weekend prior. Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster is the second-biggest movie of the year, as well as the highest-grossing R-rated movie of all time, with $539 million in North America and $1.44 billion worldwide to date.

articles.title: ‘Seduction,’ Helmed by Zelito Viana and Marcos Palmeira, to Premiere at the Inffinito Fest in Miami (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: GRAMADO, Brazil — “Seduction” (“Sedução”), a feature set in the Amazon Rainforest region and helmed by Zelito Viana and Marcos Palmeira, will have its world premiere on Sept. 11 at the 30th edition of the Inffinito Brazilian Film Festival in Miami.
body: “Seduction” marks the debut as a helmer of Marcos Palmeira, a major actor who starred in dozens of telenovelas, series and films in Brazil over the past 50 years. He toplines and co-directs the pic along with his father Zelito Viana, a vet producer of Cinema Novo classic films and director of several features, such as “Villa-Lobos: A Life of Passion.”

In the plot, Paulo (Palmeira), a renowned actor, when he learns of his father’s death in the Amazon Rainforest, embarks on a journey to settle his father’s unfinished affairs, faces the rough reality of the region and undergoing a radical transformation.

“In my opinion it is the best film of Zelito Viana, even better than ‘Villa-Lobos: A Life of Passion,’” Peregrino told Variety. “And it is fair to say, and I believe Zelito will agree with me, that Marcos’ direction work brought a freshness to the film.”
Peregrino stressed the high production value of the pic, lensed in Alter do Chão, in the Amazon region, along the Tapajós River. The pics deals with local issues, such as illegal land grabbing.

articles.title: Dr. Dre Says the Only People Who See AI as a Threat Are Those ‘Who Have Trouble Creating’
articles.summary: Dr. Dre, the legendary hip-hop producer and performer, sees AI as another tool in the music-tech toolbox akin to synthesizers — and asserted that only people “who have trouble creating” are afraid of AI.
body: Dre said he’s using AI tech in music “as a tool to see what it would do with what I just did.” Iovine added, “So is Timbaland — another brilliant producer. By the way, there’s a lot of closet AI producers out there.”
Asked what he most recently asked an AI chatbot, Dre said his query was, “How do you put on muscle and lose fat at the same time? That’s it.”

Dre, 61, was named to Forbes’ 2026 Billionaires list, joining the publication’s rankings for the first time, with an estimated net worth of $1 billion. In 2014, he and Iovine sold Beats by Dre to Apple in a deal worth more than $3 billion. Dre in 2023 sold a collection of music income streams and other assets to Shamrock Holdings and Universal Music Group for more than $200 million.

articles.title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
articles.summary: The final film in the folk horror trilogy brings closure to the saga as well as its creator's family after more than 50 years.
body: Robin Hardy always envisaged his iconic 1973 folk horror film The Wicker Man as the first part of a trilogy.
The Wicker Tree, released in 2011, brought him closer to that ambition, but his death in 2016 at the age of 86 left the project incomplete.
Now his sons, Justin and Dominic, have been able to complete their father's trilogy, after finding a script for the final film.
Wrath of the Gods has its premiere at the FrightFest horror festival in London, external on Friday, a family dream made possible thanks to the surprise discovery of some long-lost family archive.

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Hits No. 6 All-Time Globally as It Swings to Fourth Box Office Victory
articles.summary: Tom Holland's superhero blockbuster topped the worldwide sum for 'Force Awakens' while up against the launches of 'Insidious: Out of the Further' and Jason Statham's 'Mutiny.'
body: Spider-Man: Brand New Day continues to deliver in its fourth weekend at the box office after facing off against newcomers Insidious: Out of the Further and the Jason Statham -led Mutiny.

Additionally, Brand New Day becomes the No. 6 release of all time at the worldwide box office with $2.22 billion. This surpasses 2015’s Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens, which moves to seventh on the chart with $2.07 billion. The latest Spidey film is now just behind Titanic at No. 5 with $2.26 billion and Ne Zha 2 at No. 4 with $2.27 billion.

Insidious: Out of the Further occupies second place with an opening weekend of $25.3 million for the sixth installment in the horror franchise. The series hails from Screen Gems, Stage 6 Films and Blumhouse Atomic Monster and kicked off with 2011’s original Insidious. Without major studio horror releases for the next four weeks, Out of the Further aims to extend its run with limited competition. It earned a C+ CinemaScore, tying 2023’s Insidious: The Red Door for the series’ lowest grade.

articles.title: Charlize Theron Reflects on ‘Mad Max: Fury Road’ a Decade Later: “There’s a Deep Connection to This Film”
articles.summary: At a special 'Fury Road' screening, the star acknowledged how iconic her character has become, so much so that she now meets young children named Furiosa: "The weirdest thing ever."
body: Ahead of her upcoming honor at the Academy Museum Gala this fall, Charlize Theron stopped by the museum on Saturday night for a discussion about one of her biggest — and most famously fraught — projects, in Mad Max: Fury Road.

At the event, Theron was interviewed on stage by Shyla Corona and Kamila Gomez, two members of the Academy Museum Teen Council, ahead of a Fury Road screening. They touched on the star’s character preparation process and her 2004 Oscar win for Monster, as Theron began to cry, reflecting on her journey from a small town in South Africa to the Oscar stage. “It doesn’t make sense, you know,” Theron said as she wiped away tears, teasing the teen moderators, “You guys suck. I have my daughters here tonight; they can’t see me cry.” She added of her Academy Awards moment, “It’s a true testament that dreams come true, you know. And if it can happen to me, trust me, it can happen to anybody.”

articles.title: Drive-in cinemas are rare these days. But the last one in Melbourne’s north still draws a faithful crowd
articles.summary: The drive-in demands little of its audience. You can lie down, bring your dog and talk without fear of being hushed. Mridula Amin spent a night at one of the last of a dying breed. Between a funeral parlour and a sink factory, a queue of cars slowly disappears down a driveway.
body: “There’s something about watching a film under the stars, in the night air,” says Michael O’Neill, a car detailer who lives in Echuca, a five-hour return trip from the Coburg Drive-In.
At the peak of their popularity, there were more than 300 drive-in cinemas in Australia. Now, the Coburg Drive-In is the last one left within an hour of the Melbourne CBD.
O’Neil has been coming to the drive-in for 20 years, and when the light-up sign comes into view, it’s not unlike the feeling of coming home. He visits monthly.

People back home have often jeered, telling him it’s a waste of time. But O’Neill finds the traditional cinema experience lacklustre, “sat in a dark room, with phones buzzing and people talking”. He wants to live the drive-in experience while he can.

articles.title: US rapper BigXthaPlug arrested on drug and gun charges
articles.summary: The rapper, who has faced similar charges in the past, had been due to perform at the Country Rising Festival.
body: Dallas rapper BigXthaPlug has been arrested in the US state of Texas on charges of driving while intoxicated, possession of marijuana and illegal possession of a firearm.
Allen County Police confirmed to BBC Newsbeat the 28-year-old, whose real name is Xavier Landum, was stopped on Friday. He was held in Collin County Jail and later released.
Separately, he is on bail following an arrest on similar charges a year ago.
The rap artist, who makes southern hip-hop, trap, and country-rap, became well known for viral singles Texas, The Largest, and Mmhmm.

articles.summary: Which Marvel movies do Letterboxd users love the most? We've rounded up the highest rated titles, and you might be surprised by some of the entries.
body: It's no secret that Marvel superheroes as seen on film have had their share of ups and downs. From the original attempts at Captain America and Hulk in the '70s and '80s to the Avengers becoming the biggest cultural-dominating force this side of Y2K, it's been a process for studios and filmmakers to properly adapt the colorful and often unconstrained experience of reading comic books onto the big screen.

From the MCU ( which we ranked all of ) to standalone entries to more offshoot projects, there's a bevy of Marvel-related projects to dig your teeth into, but today we're asking which ones audiences have responded to the most. Specifically, what are the highest-rated Marvel movies on Letterboxd?

articles.title: AT&T Commercial Actress Milana Vayntrub Loves One Thing About Playing Marvel's Squirrel Girl
articles.summary: Milana Vayntrub missed out on getting to play Marvel's Squirrel Girl in live-action, but she adores portraying the hero in animated form, and for good reason.
body: Actor and comedian Milana Vayntrub began her professional screen acting career in 1995 when she appeared on a few episodes of the hit TV medical drama "ER." She was only about eight at the time. As we all may know, Vayntrub later became recognized worldwide when she began appearing in a series of TV ads for AT&T in 2013, playing the helpful clerk Lily.

While the ads brought Vayntrub a lot of career exposure, they also attracted a new audience of weirdo creeps. At first, a lot of the comments about Vayntrub were seemingly innocuous, with some blogs calling her the day's "hot ad girl." Unfortunately, a lot of the comments turned pretty gross pretty fast, and both AT&T and Vayntrub had to block comments and ask for the harassment to cease.

Luckily, Vayntrub continued to work during her AT&T stint, appearing in shows like "Other Space" and "@midnight," as well as films like "Ghostbusters" (2016) and, more notably, the acclaimed horror comedy video game movie "Werewolves Within." She's since appeared in the hit sci-fi film "Project Hail Mary."
points: Milana Vayntrub missed out on getting to play Marvel's Squirrel Girl in live-action, but she adores portraying the hero in animated form, and for good reason.
